source: Aamodt and Plaza (1994) Case-Based Reasoning: Foundational Issues, Methodological Variations, and System Approaches
finding: Founding statement of the cycle. CBR is both a reasoning method and a learning paradigm: learning is a by-product of solving, because each solved or failed problem is retained.
numbers: No experiments. Survey of systems. Cycle named Retrieve, Reuse, Revise, Retain.
quote: Learning in CBR occurs as a natural by-product of problem solving.
limits: Conceptual framework, not tested. Says effective retention still needs methods to extract, integrate and index the case.
agent_relevance: Gives the loop for the memory part of the schema. Retain is not free: it needs extraction and indexing rules, and a failure must store its reason, not only the outcome.

source: Lopez de Mantaras, McSherry, Bridge, Leake, Smyth et al. (2005) Retrieval, reuse, revision and retention in case-based reasoning
finding: Twenty-year review of the four Rs. The early view that every episode should be retained proved naive. Case-base growth raises retrieval cost (the utility problem), so selective retention and maintenance became a field.
numbers: No single experiment. Cites Smyth and Cunningham 1996: mean retrieval time degrades with case-base size while adaptation savings improve at a decreasing rate, so there is a critical size past which total efficiency falls.
quote: learning would occur as a by-product of every problem solving episode
limits: Review. The utility result is shown under general assumptions, not for LLM agents.
agent_relevance: Direct warning for Retain. Write a case only when it adds new coverage. Cap or prune the bank. Later LLM papers (c05, c10) find the same limit.

source: Zhou, Chen, Guo et al. (2025) Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
finding: A planner-executor LLM agent built as an explicit CBR loop (Retrieve, Reuse and Revise, Evaluate, Retain) with a case bank and a learned retrieval policy (soft Q-learning). Reaches top GAIA validation with no weight updates.
numbers: GAIA validation 87.88 percent Pass@3 (Level 1 96.23, Level 2 90.70, Level 3 61.54); test 79.40 percent using the bank built on validation. DeepResearcher seven sets: 66.6 F1 and 80.4 PM. SimpleQA 95.0 PM. HLE 24.4 PM. Planner GPT-4.1, executor o3 (GAIA) or o4-mini.
quote: case-based memory adds 4.7% to 9.6% absolute points on out-of-distribution tasks
limits: Leaderboard claims by the authors. Executor is a strong reasoning model. Planning and live tools account for most of the gain (see c04). Test result depends on a bank grown on validation questions.
agent_relevance: Best recent proof that the 4R loop can run around a frozen model. It adds learned retrieval, which our code-only schema may replace with a counted rule.

source: Memento (2025) component ablation, Table 5
finding: The CBR memory adds a smaller, consistent increment on top of planning. Planning without CBR gives most of the gain. Live search alone can hurt.
numbers: Adding CBR to planning: HLE +4.5 F1 / +7.0 PM; SimpleQA +3.7 / +5.3; DeepResearcher +6.7 / +8.2. Planning without CBR: HLE +11.0 / +1.6; SimpleQA +32.5 / +4.9; DeepResearcher +29.1 / +11.5. Live tools without planning on DeepResearcher: -18.0 F1 / -2.1 PM.
limits: Single run per cell, no confidence intervals reported. Authors suspect contamination on DeepResearcher sets.
agent_relevance: Size the memory expectation honestly: about 4 to 8 points, not a revolution. Control and planning matter more.

source: Memento (2025) number of retrieved cases K and learning curves, Tables 3 and 4
finding: Few retrieved cases are best. More cases do not help and slightly hurt. Performance grows over five passes as the bank fills, with diminishing returns.
numbers: DeepResearcher average F1/PM: K=0 59.9/72.2; K=1 63.6/77.9; K=4 64.5/78.5 (best); K=16 63.9/78.1; K=32 63.9/78.1. Five-iteration accuracy: no CBR 78.65 to 84.47; non-parametric CBR 79.84 to 84.85; parametric CBR 80.46 to 85.44.
quote: CBR benefits from a small, high-quality memory, unlike few-shot prompting
limits: Gap between CBR and no-CBR shrinks to under 1 point by iteration 5 (84.47 vs 84.85 non-parametric). The same questions are replayed across iterations, so part of the curve is repetition.
agent_relevance: Retrieve about 4 cases, not 30. Expect most of the lift early. Matches the utility-problem warning in c02.

source: Zhao, Huang, Xu, Lin, Liu, Huang (2024) ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners (AAAI)
finding: Agent gathers trajectories, extracts natural-language insights (abstraction) and retrieves similar successful trajectories (reuse). Both parts help and they are synergistic.
numbers: gpt-3.5-turbo, four-fold validation. Insights-only / retrieve-only: HotpotQA 36 / 31; ALFWorld 50 / 55; WebShop 37 / 38 percent. Full ExpeL ALFWorld 59.0 vs ReAct 40.0. HotpotQA 39.0 vs ReAct 28.0.
limits: Weak base model. Small test folds. ExpeL without retries roughly matches Reflexion with retries on HotpotQA (40 vs 39 at R3).
agent_relevance: Store both a concrete case and an abstracted rule. Concrete cases win when the task needs exact action sequences. Insights win for general question types.

source: ExpeL (2024) ablations on retrieval ranking and insight source, Table 3 and Table 1
finding: How you index matters. Retrieval by task similarity beats retrieval by latest-reasoning similarity, which beats random successful trajectories. Insights built with reflections hurt. Insights transfer across tasks.
numbers: ALFWorld SR: ReAct 40.0; random sampled successes 42.5; reasoning-similarity 48.5; task-similarity (ExpeL) 59.0. HotpotQA: hand-crafted insights 32.0; insights built with reflections 29.0; gpt-3.5 insights 32.0; ExpeL 39.0. FEVER transfer from HotpotQA insights: Act 58, ReAct 63, transfer without task demos 65, with demos 70.
limits: One benchmark per ablation, standard errors from four folds only.
agent_relevance: Indexing is the case-based part that carries the effect: random retrieval is almost as bad as no memory (42.5 vs 40). Index by task, not by the current thought.

source: Shinn, Cassano, Berman, Gopinath, Narasimhan, Yao (2023) Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
finding: Retain plus revise inside one task family: failed attempts produce a verbal reflection stored in an episodic buffer and used in the next trial. Needs an external success signal.
numbers: AlfWorld: ReAct+Reflexion completes 130 of 134 tasks over 12 trials; ReAct alone plateaus between trials 6 and 7. Gains over baselines: +22 points AlfWorld, +20 HotPotQA, +11 HumanEval. HumanEval pass@1 91 vs GPT-4 80.
limits: Needs binary or test feedback. Reflection alone can fail to fix hallucination loops (paper reports a 22 percent hallucination rate with no recovery in one ablation). Same-task retries, not a case base across tasks.
agent_relevance: Supports G2: revise from real output. The signal source (tests, environment) is what makes the retained note useful.

source: Wang, Mao, Fried, Neubig (2024) Agent Workflow Memory
finding: Retain at the level of reusable workflows (abstracted sub-routines) rather than raw trajectories, induced offline or online, then given to the agent. Gains grow when train and test tasks differ more.
numbers: WebArena with gpt-4: 35.5 percent overall success vs BrowserGym 23.5 (51.1 percent relative, +12.0 absolute); beats human-written workflows (SteP, 32.0) by 7.6 to 7.9 percent relative. Mind2Web cross-task +24.6 percent relative step success. Gap over baseline widens from 8.9 to 14.0 absolute points as train-test distance grows.
limits: Online mode induces workflows from the agent's own, possibly wrong, test runs using an evaluator. gpt-4 at temperature 0. WebArena has only test tasks.
agent_relevance: Abstract the case into a routine before storing. Good fit for our agent, where operators are already named routines.

source: Xiong, Lin, Xie et al. (2025) How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: experience-following behavior
finding: Agents copy retrieved cases: when the retrieved input is close to the query, the output is close to the retrieved output. This helps with good cases and spreads errors with bad ones. Strict-evaluator addition and history-based deletion improve long-run performance.
numbers: Output similarity rises with input similarity across four agents. Add-all and loose-evaluator addition widen the gap to an error-free-memory baseline over time. History-based deletion with a strict evaluator on AgentDriver can beat the error-free baseline. Fixed-size memory of 100 (EHRAgent) and 180 (AgentDriver) records still gains with utility-based deletion.
limits: Exact percentages sit in figures, not text. Evaluator quality drives everything. One agent is synthetic (RegAgent).
agent_relevance: Strongest evidence for gating Retain: store only checked-correct cases and delete cases whose later use did not help. Later task results are free labels.

source: Sarukkai, Xie, Fatahalian (2025) Self-Generated In-Context Examples Improve LLM Agents for Sequential Decision-Making Tasks
finding: Plain retain-successes-only plus retrieve works. Curating the database and individual exemplars adds more. Gains match or exceed a model upgrade.
numbers: gpt-4o-mini, top-k retrieval (k=6 ALFWorld and InterCode-SQL, 10 Wordcraft). Naive bootstrap: ALFWorld 73 to 89, Wordcraft 55 to 64, InterCode-SQL 75 to 79. With database-level and exemplar-level curation ALFWorld 93 (0.93 plus or minus 0.03 at 3500 tasks). The 15-point boost is similar to upgrading gpt-4o-mini to gpt-4o and matches allowing multiple attempts.
limits: Diminishing returns with bank size. Large trial-to-trial variance (five trials differ). Curation dips at small bank sizes from noisy utility estimates.
agent_relevance: Retain only successes, then measure each case by how it helps later tasks (empirical utility) and prune. Report variance across seeds.

source: Suzgun, Yuksekgonul, Bianchi, Jurafsky, Zou (2025) Dynamic Cheatsheet: Test-Time Learning with Adaptive Memory
finding: A self-curated text memory (retain) with optional similarity retrieval and synthesis (DC-RS) lifts strong models, but the biggest jumps come from storing working code, and small models gain little.
numbers: Claude 3.5 Sonnet AIME 2024: baseline 23.3, empty-memory scaffold 36.7, cumulative memory 50.0, retrieval and synthesis 46.7. AIME 2025: 6.7, 23.3, 36.7, 30.0. GPT-4o Game of 24: baseline 10.0, empty scaffold 19.0, cumulative 93.0, retrieval and synthesis 99.0. GPT-4o MMLU-Pro Engineering: baseline 53.2, cumulative 44.0 (worse). Claude GPQA-Diamond 59.6 to 68.7 (RS).
limits: AIME sets have 30 questions, so one question is 3.3 points. Much of the Game of 24 gain is discovering a Python solution once. The empty-memory scaffold already gives large gains, so read memory effect against it.
agent_relevance: Always compare against the same scaffold with empty memory. Memory helps most when a reusable procedure or tool exists.

source: Dynamic Cheatsheet (2025) limits for smaller models, Table 3
finding: Smaller models cannot curate or use memory well. They fill it with flawed strategies and struggle to refine stored content.
numbers: Claude 3.5 Haiku AIME 2025: baseline 0.0, empty scaffold 13.3, cumulative 13.3, retrieval and synthesis 10.0 (no gain from memory over the scaffold alone). GPT-4o-mini gains even smaller.
limits: Few items, 2024 models.
agent_relevance: Memory depends on model strength. Our evidence gate (code check before store) matters more for weaker models.

source: Ouyang, Yan, Hsu et al. (2025/2026) ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
finding: Store distilled strategies from both successes and failures (judged by an LLM), not raw trajectories. Beats no memory, Synapse (raw trajectories) and AWM (success-only workflows). Memory-aware test-time scaling adds more.
numbers: WebArena overall success, Gemini-2.5-flash: no memory 40.5, Synapse 42.1, AWM 44.1, ReasoningBank 48.8, plus scaling 51.8; steps 9.7 to 8.3. Shopping subset 39.0 to 49.7. Mind2Web cross-task SR 3.3 to 4.8, cross-website 1.7 to 2.3 (very low base). Gemma-3-12B WebArena-Shopping: 17.1 no memory, Synapse 16.0, AWM 21.4, ReasoningBank 24.1.
limits: Authors are from a model vendor. Judge was only 72.7 percent accurate against ground truth, yet results held for simulated judge accuracy 70 to 90 percent. Mind2Web gains are tiny in absolute SR.
agent_relevance: Raw trajectory storage (Synapse) barely helped or hurt on a small model. Distilled strategies did better.

source: ReasoningBank (2025) failure-inclusion ablation and judge noise, Figures 7 and 8
finding: Adding failure trajectories improved ReasoningBank but not other methods. Retain stays robust to noisy success labels.
numbers: WebArena-Shopping, Gemini-2.5-flash: no memory 39.0; ReasoningBank success-only 46.5 vs with failures 49.7. Other methods in the figure gave 41.7 to 44.4 (AWM with failures read as lower, pairing uncertain). Simulated judge accuracy 100 down to 50 percent: success rate 50.6 at 100, about 47.6 at 50.
limits: Figure values read from axis labels, so exact pairing of values to bars is uncertain. One subset.
agent_relevance: Failure notes only helped when distilled into a strategy. Dumping failed trajectories can hurt.

source: Tang, Qin, Peng et al. (2025) Agent KB: Leveraging Cross-Domain Experience for Agentic Problem Solving
finding: A shared case base across agent frameworks, with two-stage retrieval (planning workflows, then error-fix feedback) and a disagreement gate so retrieved cases do not override the agent when they conflict.
numbers: smolagents on GAIA pass@3 55.2 to 73.9 (+18.7 points). OpenHands SWE-bench pass@1 24.3 to 28.3 (+4.0). Ablations say hybrid retrieval and both stages are needed and that auto-generated experiences match manual curation.
limits: Only abstract and introduction read this session. Pass@3 can include selection luck.
agent_relevance: The disagreement gate answers case interference. It fits G4: a retrieved case is a hint, not proof.

source: Wiratunga, Abeyratne, Jayawardena et al. (2024) CBR-RAG: Case-Based Reasoning for Retrieval Augmented Generation in LLMs for Legal QA
finding: Uses only the Retrieve stage of the cycle, with case structure (question, support, full case) and hybrid embeddings. Gains over no retrieval are small and the metric is weak.
numbers: Mistral-7B, 32 test cases, Australian legal QA. Answer-to-reference cosine: No-RAG 0.8967; best hybrid AnglEBERT k=3 full case 0.9141 (about 1.94 percent increase; significant against No-RAG and hybrid LegalBERT at 95 percent, against hybrid BERT k=1 at 90 percent). Best retrieval F1 setting: weights [0.25, 0.40, 0.35], k=3.
limits: Only 32 test cases. Cosine similarity to a reference is not correctness; no expert review. No-RAG baseline already high.
agent_relevance: Structured case indexing helps a little. Also shows how weak the evaluation of CBR-style RAG often is.

source: Hu, Tang, Yang, Zhang (2024) Case-Based or Rule-Based: How Do Transformers Do the Math?
finding: Tests whether the model itself reasons by cases or by rules. A Leave-Square-Out intervention shows transformers behave as case-based reasoners on addition-like tasks, with near zero accuracy on held-out regions. Teaching rules explicitly fixes it.
numbers: Fine-tuned on 1 to 5 digit addition, Rule-Following Fine-Tuning generalizes to up to 12 digits with over 95 percent accuracy, over 40 points higher than scratchpad. Held-out Leave-Square-Out regions show almost zero accuracy.
limits: Small fine-tuned models plus pretrained LLMs on arithmetic. Not about prompting memory.
agent_relevance: A reason to pair retrieved cases with an explicit rule or check: the model alone tends to interpolate cases, not apply rules.

source: Yang, Yu, Zhang et al. (2024) Buffer of Thoughts: Thought-Augmented Reasoning with Large Language Models
finding: Retain and reuse at template level: distilled thought-templates in a meta-buffer, retrieved and instantiated per problem, with a buffer manager that updates the store.
numbers: Ten tasks. Claimed gains over previous best: +11 percent Game of 24, +20 Geometric Shapes, +51 Checkmate-in-One. Table rows: Game of 24 GPT-4 3.0 vs BoT 82.4; Geometric Shapes 52.6 vs 93.6; Checkmate-in-One 36.4 vs 86.4. About 12 percent of the cost of multi-query methods.
limits: Tasks come in repeated template families, which favours template reuse. Small BIG-Bench style test sets.
agent_relevance: Template reuse is cheap when the task family repeats. Check that your eval does not repeat families more than real use.

source: Wang, Xie, Jiang et al. (2023) Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
finding: A skill library of executable code with iterative prompting (environment feedback, execution errors, self-verification) acts as retain plus revise for a black-box GPT-4 agent. Skills transfer to a new world.
numbers: Abstract and method section read only. Numeric comparisons not extracted this session.
limits: Minecraft, one environment. Skills are executable code that can be verified, which is why retention is safe.
agent_relevance: Verified, executable cases are the safe form of retained memory.

source: Cross-paper comparison of c03, c06, c11, c12, c14
finding: Across 2023-2025 LLM-agent memory papers the same pattern repeats: memory gives small to moderate gains (about 4 to 19 points) on agentic tasks, large gains only where a reusable executable procedure exists, and quality of what is stored matters more than quantity.
numbers: Gains: Memento CBR +4.7 to 9.6 OOD; ExpeL +19 ALFWorld (40 to 59); Sarukkai +16 ALFWorld (73 to 89); ReasoningBank +8.3 WebArena overall; Dynamic Cheatsheet Game of 24 +83 (code reuse). Useful k: about 4 (Memento) to 6 (Sarukkai).
limits: Different base models, benchmarks and baselines. Not a meta-analysis. None of these is independently replicated.
agent_relevance: Plan for modest gains and test against an empty-memory control with the same scaffold. Store procedures and checks over narrative.

source: Memento (2025) mapping of the 4R cycle into an LLM loop, Definition 3.2 and Algorithm 1
finding: Explicit mapping of the Aamodt-Plaza cycle to an LLM agent: Retrieve is a learned case-selection policy, Reuse and Revise is the LLM acting on state plus retrieved case, Evaluation is an environment reward, Retain appends state, action and reward to the case bank.
numbers: Case bank M(t+1) = M(t) plus the new (state, action, reward) tuple. Retrieval is a softmax over learned Q values with one-step temporal-difference learning and a state-similarity term.
limits: Authors leave part of the cycle (a separate Evaluation and case revision stage) for future work.
agent_relevance: Revise is left to the model here. Our schema insists revision cite real failing output (G2), which is stricter.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) misaligned experience replay and distribution shift sections
finding: Even stored cases that passed a quality filter can mislead later tasks. Retained demonstrations show lower error than deleted ones. Under task-distribution shift, periodic deletion keeps the agent near its no-shift level.
numbers: Under shift on AgentDriver, strict addition alone matched or beat the no-shift variant; on EHRAgent history-based deletion alone underperformed combined deletion. Records with error above 0.5 still propagated errors after strict addition (error at most 1 filter).
limits: Numeric tables are mostly in figures. Evaluator error and distribution mismatch are mixed.
agent_relevance: Aging and deleting cases matters. Add a drop rule for cases that were retrieved and did not help.

source: Sarukkai et al. (2025) variance and curation findings
finding: Databases built the same way by different random runs give different results, so single-run claims for retain-and-reuse are unreliable. Population-based selection of databases reduces this.
numbers: Five InterCode-SQL trials differ visibly (about 0.72 to 0.78 on the figure axis). Database-level curation replaces the worst database with a copy of the best on a rolling window. Dips at small sizes come from low sample counts.
limits: Axis readings from a figure, not a table.
agent_relevance: Run several seeds before believing a memory gain. Do not prune on few observations.

source: Aamodt and Plaza (1994) read against ExpeL (concrete case versus abstraction)
finding: Aamodt and Plaza say it is usually easier to learn by retaining a concrete experience than to generalize. LLM results support both sides: concrete cases led on ALFWorld (retrieve-only 55 vs insights-only 50), abstraction led on HotpotQA (insights-only 36 vs retrieve-only 31).
numbers: ExpeL numbers as in c06.
quote: easier to learn by retaining a concrete problem solving experience than to generalize from it
limits: One lab, one base model (gpt-3.5).
agent_relevance: Keep concrete cases as the base store and add a small set of checked abstractions on top.

source: Lopez de Mantaras et al. (2005) harmful cases and selective retention
finding: Remedies for harmful or redundant cases come from nearest-neighbour editing: Hart condensed NN (remove redundancy, 1968) and Wilson edited NN (remove noise, 1972), plus competence models of the case base.
numbers: No numbers read this session for these methods; historical citations only.
limits: Pre-LLM. Embeddings change the geometry, but the redundancy and noise ideas still apply.
agent_relevance: Two cheap code rules for our bank: skip a new case if a near-identical one exists; drop a case if its neighbours disagree with its label.

source: Agent Workflow Memory (2024) online learning curve
finding: Online workflow learning improves quickly. The gap over the baseline reaches as high as 22.5 points on a WebArena split after only tens of examples, and the agent needs fewer steps.
numbers: Gap up to 22.5 points on a WebArena subset after tens of examples (text claim). Total success 35.5 vs 23.5 for the BrowserGym baseline.
limits: Table rows in the text extraction were scrambled, so subset values were not checked cell by cell.
agent_relevance: Early gain then plateau: expect a short learning phase.

source: Reflexion (2023) plateau of repeated attempts
finding: Without reflection memory, the plain ReAct agent stops improving after several retries. With reflection memory it keeps solving more tasks over 12 trials.
numbers: ReAct-only plateau between trials 6 and 7 on AlfWorld; ReAct plus Reflexion solves 130 of 134 tasks.
limits: A heuristic hallucination and inefficiency detector triggers the reflection.
agent_relevance: Retain a lesson only after a detected failure signal, in line with G1.
